## Facts (4):
- [hazard] Email provider: sandbox behaviour and limits (id: 01a10b2d-bdda-7cb1-9cd2-adfcbd5f3b9d; source: shared/human)
  The notifier sends through the email provider's HTTP API (provider.send). Production credentials exist only in the deployed function's environment. For development there is a separate sandbox account whose key is in the dev secrets store; export it as MAIL_API_KEY. The sandbox has the same API and response shapes, but it is rate-limited to 2 messages per second and capped at 500 messages a day for the whole team, so do not loop over large fixtures. Bounces and complaints are simulated with magic addresses from the provider's docs. Important: the sandbox silently drops (answers 202, never delivers) every message whose recipient is not on the `@sink.acme.test` domain, so a test that asserts delivery must send to an address such as `receipts@sink.acme.test` and read it back from the sink inbox API.
- [convention] Notifier email templates (id: 01a10b2d-91fe-79d0-aef1-b2388e428d57; source: shared/human)
  Email templates live in services/notifier/templates/ as `<event>.mjml` and are compiled at build time. Every template needs a plain-text twin `<event>.txt` with the same variables, because some corporate mail gateways strip HTML. Template variables are snake_case.
- [context] Who owns the notifier (current) (id: 01a10b2d-d7ee-7ac3-925c-97343b6abed9; source: shared/human)
  As of 2026-09-01 the notifier belongs to the Growth team (Dana Okafor moved to Platform). Template and copy changes are signed off in #growth-eng; any Growth engineer can approve.
- [convention] Feature flags in the notifier (id: 01a10b2e-191d-7642-b1e1-51d6bc3e5500; source: shared/human)
  The notifier is deployed separately and cannot read the root flags.toml. Its flags are environment variables named `NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>` (upper snake case, value "1" to enable), read with `os.environ.get("NOTIFIER_FF_<NAME>") == "1"`.","hookEventName":"PreToolUse"}}

Mostly nothing was blocked, but one thing was awkward.

- **Conflicting memories with no scope shown.** The prompt hook injected two memories that pull in opposite directions. One said never to edit files in `migrations/` and to add a new numbered file instead. The other said the notifier's migrations are unapplied, so edit them in place until launch. I settled it by reading the text: the first names the root `migrations/` directory and a 4-digit numbering scheme, and the second names `services/notifier/migrations/` and timestamped names. The injected context didn't show each memory's `physical` scope or whether either had been superseded or challenged. I would have wanted those fields in the hook output, for example `physical: ["migrations/"]` on the hazard. A `query` call with `path` set to the migration file might have given the same information, but I didn't try it.

- **No memory calls this session.** I made no EngramDB calls, so I can't say whether `query`, `create` or `challenge` would have fallen short. The session-end hook suggested reflecting on the session. I judged that nothing durable had come up, so I skipped it. The memory tools were also unavailable by the time of this debrief, so I couldn't have used them anyway.

- **Can't check whether a migration was applied.** The "not applied to any shared database" claim rests entirely on a memory. EngramDB has nothing that could confirm it, and it shouldn't. A `verify`-style check against the repo or deploy state would have been useful, but that is outside what a memory store can do.
